      #### functions ####

      drop_index <- function(x, k) {
        n <- length(x)
        out <- rep(NA_integer_, n - 1)
        j <- 1
        for (i in seq_len(n)) {
          if (i != k) {
            out[j] <- x[i]
            j <- j + 1
          }
        }
        return(out)
      }
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      k <- dat$k  # number of rows
      p <- dat$p  # number of columns
      row_id <- dat$row_id  # row indices 
      col_id <- dat$col_id  # column indices
      cell_id <- dat$cell_id  # cell indices
      count <- dat$count
      ref_row <- dat$ref_row  # reference for 0-row effect
      ref_col <- dat$ref_col  # reference for 0-column effect
      ref_cell <- dat$ref_cell  # reference for 0-interaction effect
      gamma_sd_sd <- dat$gamma_sd_sd  # standard deviation for the interactions cale
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### transformed data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      kp <- k * p
      row_inds <- rep(NA_integer_, k)
      for (i in seq_len(k)) {
        row_inds[i] <- i
      }
      col_inds <- rep(NA_integer_, p)
      for (i in seq_len(p)) {
        col_inds[i] <- i
      }
      cell_inds <- rep(NA_integer_, kp)
      for (i in seq_len(kp)) {
        cell_inds[i] <- i
      }
      nref_row <- drop_index(row_inds, ref_row)
      nref_col <- drop_index(col_inds, ref_col)
      nref_cell <- drop_index(cell_inds, ref_cell)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      alpha_raw <- rep(NA_real_, k - 1)  # row intercepts
      alpha_sd <- NA_real_
      beta_raw <- rep(NA_real_, p - 1)  # col intercepts
      beta_sd <- NA_real_
      gamma_raw <- rep(NA_real_, kp - 1)  # interaction effects
      gamma_sd <- NA_real_
      # priors
      alpha_raw <- rnorm(length(alpha_raw))
      beta_raw <- rnorm(length(beta_raw))
      gamma_raw <- rnorm(length(gamma_raw))
      alpha_sd <- abs(rnorm(1))
      beta_sd <- abs(rnorm(1))
      gamma_sd <- abs(rnorm(1))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### transformed parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      alpha <- rep(NA_real_, k)  # row effects
      alpha[ref_row] <- 0  # fix "largest" entry for identifiability
      alpha[nref_row] <- alpha_raw * alpha_sd
      
      beta <- rep(NA_real_, p)  # column effects
      beta[ref_col] <- 0  # fix "largest" entry for identifiability
      beta[nref_col] <- beta_raw * beta_sd
      
      gamma <- rep(NA_real_, kp)  # interaction effects
      gamma[ref_cell] <- 0  # fix "largest" entry for identifiability
      gamma[nref_cell] <- gamma_raw * gamma_sd * gamma_sd_sd
      
      eta <- alpha[row_id] + beta[col_id] + gamma[cell_id]  # construct latents
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      # likelihood
      count <- as.vector(rmultinom(1, size = sum(count), prob = softmax(eta)))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### generated quantities ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      # recover centered parameters (to accommodate fixing for identifiability)
      alpha_centered <- alpha - mean(alpha)
      beta_centered <- beta - mean(beta)
      gamma_centered <- gamma - mean(gamma)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      out <- list(k = k, p = p, row_id = row_id, col_id = col_id, cell_id = cell_id,
        count = count, ref_row = ref_row, ref_col = ref_col, ref_cell = ref_cell,
        gamma_sd_sd = gamma_sd_sd, kp = kp, row_inds = row_inds, col_inds = col_inds,
        cell_inds = cell_inds, nref_row = nref_row, nref_col = nref_col, nref_cell = nref_cell,
        alpha_raw = alpha_raw, alpha_sd = alpha_sd, beta_raw = beta_raw, beta_sd = beta_sd,
        gamma_raw = gamma_raw, gamma_sd = gamma_sd, alpha = alpha, beta = beta, gamma = gamma,
        eta = eta, alpha_centered = alpha_centered, beta_centered = beta_centered,
        gamma_centered = gamma_centered)

# translation of correlation-matrix_from-bivariate-Fisher-z.stan

    Code
      cat(snapshot_text(f, "prior_predictive"))
    Output
      # R translation of a Stan program, generated by Stan2R (prior predictive simulation).
      # Reads data from the list `dat`; every top-level Stan variable is returned in `out`.
      
      # helper functions
      # onion method (Lewandowski, Kurowicka and Joe 2009); returns the lower Cholesky factor
      rlkj_corr_cholesky <- function(like, eta) {
        K <- nrow(like)
        if (K == 1) return(matrix(1, 1, 1))
        alpha <- eta + (K - 2) / 2
        r12 <- 2 * rbeta(1, alpha, alpha) - 1
        R <- matrix(0, K, K)
        R[1, 1] <- 1
        R[1, 2] <- r12
        R[2, 2] <- sqrt(1 - r12^2)
        if (K > 2) {
          for (m in 2:(K - 1)) {
            alpha <- alpha - 0.5
            y <- rbeta(1, m / 2, alpha)
            z <- rnorm(m)
            R[1:m, m + 1] <- sqrt(y) * z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
            R[m + 1, m + 1] <- sqrt(1 - y)
          }
        }
        t(R)
      }
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      p <- dat$p
      np <- dat$np
      ip <- dat$ip
      z <- dat$z
      sigma_z <- dat$sigma_z
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      # corr_matrix[p] R;
      L <- matrix(NA_real_, p, p)
      # R ~ lkj_corr(1);
      L <- rlkj_corr_cholesky(L, 1)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### transformed parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      R <- tcrossprod(L)
      Rz <- rep(NA_real_, np)
      for (i in seq_len(np)) {
        r <- R[ip[i, 1], ip[i, 2]]
        Rz[i] <- 0.5 * log((1 + r) / (1 - r))
      }
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      z <- rnorm(length(z), Rz, sigma_z)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      out <- list(p = p, np = np, ip = ip, z = z, sigma_z = sigma_z, L = L, R = R, Rz = Rz)

# translation of correlation_uncertainty_bivariate-laplace.stan

    Code

    Output
      # R translation of a Stan program, generated by Stan2R (prior predictive simulation).
      # Reads data from the list `dat`; every top-level Stan variable is returned in `out`.
      
      # helper functions
      # fill `like` (a vector, or an array of vectors stored one per row) with draws
      rmulti_normal <- function(like, mu, Sigma) {
        R <- chol(Sigma)
        if (is.matrix(like)) {
          z <- matrix(rnorm(length(like)), nrow(like), ncol(like)) %*% R
          if (is.matrix(mu)) z + mu else sweep(z, 2, mu, "+")
        } else {
          as.vector(mu + rnorm(length(like)) %*% R)
        }
      }
      # onion method (Lewandowski, Kurowicka and Joe 2009); returns the lower Cholesky factor
      rlkj_corr_cholesky <- function(like, eta) {
        K <- nrow(like)
        if (K == 1) return(matrix(1, 1, 1))
        alpha <- eta + (K - 2) / 2
        r12 <- 2 * rbeta(1, alpha, alpha) - 1
        R <- matrix(0, K, K)
        R[1, 1] <- 1
        R[1, 2] <- r12
        R[2, 2] <- sqrt(1 - r12^2)
        if (K > 2) {
          for (m in 2:(K - 1)) {
            alpha <- alpha - 0.5
            y <- rbeta(1, m / 2, alpha)
            z <- rnorm(m)
            R[1:m, m + 1] <- sqrt(y) * z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
            R[m + 1, m + 1] <- sqrt(1 - y)
          }
        }
        t(R)
      }
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      n <- dat$n
      x_err <- dat$x_err
      sd_x_err <- dat$sd_x_err
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      x <- matrix(NA_real_, n, 2)
      w <- rep(NA_real_, n)  # auxiliary variable to get bivariate exponential
      sigma_x <- rep(NA_real_, 2)
      L <- matrix(NA_real_, 2, 2)
      sigma_x <- abs(rnorm(length(sigma_x), 0, 2))
      w <- rexp(length(w), 1)
      L <- rlkj_corr_cholesky(L, 1)
      x <- rmulti_normal(x, rep(0, 2), tcrossprod(sigma_x * L))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      x_err[, 1] <- rnorm(length(x_err[, 1]), as.vector(x[, 1]) * sqrt(w), sd_x_err[, 1])
      x_err[, 2] <- rnorm(length(x_err[, 2]), as.vector(x[, 2]) * sqrt(w), sd_x_err[, 2])
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### generated quantities ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      r <- tcrossprod(L * lower.tri(L, diag = TRUE))[1, 2]
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      out <- list(n = n, x_err = x_err, sd_x_err = sd_x_err, x = x, w = w, sigma_x = sigma_x,
        L = L, r = r)

      # helper functions
      # fill `like` (a vector, or an array of vectors stored one per row) with draws
      rmulti_normal <- function(like, mu, Sigma) {
        R <- chol(Sigma)
        if (is.matrix(like)) {
          z <- matrix(rnorm(length(like)), nrow(like), ncol(like)) %*% R
          if (is.matrix(mu)) z + mu else sweep(z, 2, mu, "+")
        } else {
          as.vector(mu + rnorm(length(like)) %*% R)
        }
      }
      # onion method (Lewandowski, Kurowicka and Joe 2009); returns the lower Cholesky factor
      rlkj_corr_cholesky <- function(like, eta) {
        K <- nrow(like)
        if (K == 1) return(matrix(1, 1, 1))
        alpha <- eta + (K - 2) / 2
        r12 <- 2 * rbeta(1, alpha, alpha) - 1
        R <- matrix(0, K, K)
        R[1, 1] <- 1
        R[1, 2] <- r12
        R[2, 2] <- sqrt(1 - r12^2)
        if (K > 2) {
          for (m in 2:(K - 1)) {
            alpha <- alpha - 0.5
            y <- rbeta(1, m / 2, alpha)
            z <- rnorm(m)
            R[1:m, m + 1] <- sqrt(y) * z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
            R[m + 1, m + 1] <- sqrt(1 - y)
          }
        }
        t(R)
      }

      # sample_intersection:
      # Replicates the core logic of your R function but expects:
      # - Lambda: coefficients of the hyperellipsoid (length p).

      # Returns:

      # and the hyperellipsoid with coefficients Lambda.
      sample_intersection <- function(Lambda, y, theta, sign_flip) {

        k <- p - 2  # should match num_elements(theta)

        i_min <- 1
        i_max <- 1
        L_min <- Lambda[1]
        L_max <- Lambda[1]
        for (i in stan_range(2, p)) {
          if (Lambda[i] < L_min) {
            L_min <- Lambda[i]
            i_min <- i
          }
          if (Lambda[i] > L_max) {
            L_max <- Lambda[i]
            i_max <- i
          }
        }
        # 2) Collect the remaining (p-2) indices
        remain_index <- rep(NA_integer_, p - 2)
        idx <- 1
        for (i in seq_len(p)) {
          if ((i != i_min) && (i != i_max)) {
            remain_index[idx] <- i
            idx <- idx + 1
          }
        }
        # 3) Extract L_k (remaining) and L_drop (dropped)
        L_k <- rep(NA_real_, p - 2)
        for (i in seq_len((p - 2))) {
          L_k[i] <- Lambda[remain_index[i]]
        }

        L_drop[1] <- Lambda[i_min]
        L_drop[2] <- Lambda[i_max]
        # 4) Compute scaling factor s
        sts <- sum(theta^2)  # sum(theta^2)
        stes <- 0  # sum(L_k * theta^2)
        for (i in seq_len((p - 2))) {

        }

        sb2_sq[2] <- (L_drop[2] - 1) / (L_drop[2] * sts - stes)
        sb2_1 <- if ((sb2_sq[1] > 0)) sqrt(sb2_sq[1]) else Inf
        sb2_2 <- if ((sb2_sq[2] > 0)) sqrt(sb2_sq[2]) else Inf
        # s is the min of sa, sb1, sb2_1, sb2_2
        s <- pmin(sa, pmin(sb1, pmin(sb2_1, sb2_2)))

        x[i_min] <- x_d1
        x[i_max] <- x_d2
        for (i in seq_len((p - 2))) {
          x[remain_index[i]] <- x_k[i]
        }

      # -------------------------------------------------------------------
      # intersection_constraint:

      #   - theta: a unit_vector of dimension (prem-2)
      #   - sign_flip in {-1, 1}
      # Returns:
      #   A p x prem matrix whose:
      #       col 1 = the newly sampled vector (new_vec)
      #       cols 2..prem = the updated basis B_new
      # -------------------------------------------------------------------
      intersection_constraint <- function(L, V_curr, B_curr, y, theta, sign_flip) {
        p <- length(L)
        pcurr <- ncol(V_curr)
        prem <- p - pcurr
        # 1) Construct a suitable B
        #    If pcurr=0, replicate "B = diag(p)" logic. Otherwise use B_curr.
        B <- matrix(NA_real_, p, prem)
        if (pcurr == 0) {
          # Identity is p x p, we only need its first prem columns
          I <- diag(rep(1.0, p), nrow = length(rep(1.0, p)))
          B <- I[, seq_len(prem), drop = FALSE]
        } else {
          B <- B_curr  # assumed dimension p x prem
        }
        # 2) Q = B' * diag(L) * B, dimension (prem x prem)
        diagL <- diag(L, nrow = length(L))
        Q <- (t(B) %*% diagL) %*% B
        # 3) Eigen-decomposition of Q
        #    Stan has eigen_sym() for symmetric matrices
        QD <- rev(eigen(Q, symmetric = TRUE)$values)
        QV <- eigen(Q, symmetric = TRUE)$vectors[, rev(seq_len(nrow(Q))), drop = FALSE]
        # The order of QD is ascending if Q is positive semidefinite. 
        # We'll just use them directly; the "sample_intersection" doesn't require sorting.
        # 4) Sample a point on the intersection for the prem-dim ellipsoid QD
        #    Note: "theta" should be unit_vector[prem-2], "y" in [0,1].
        evec <- sample_intersection(QD, y, theta, sign_flip)
        # 5) Transform evec back to original space
        Qvec <- as.vector(QV %*% evec)  # still prem-dim
        new_vec <- as.vector(B %*% Qvec)  # now p-dim
        # 6) Rank-1 update for B_new
        alpha <- as.vector(t(B) %*% new_vec)  # alpha in R^prem
        B_new <- B - outer(new_vec, alpha)  # dimension p x prem
        # 7) Re-orthonormalize B_new, keep rank (prem-1)
        #    Stan has qr_thin_Q() which returns a p x prem matrix with orthonormal columns
        Q_temp <- qr_thin_Q(B_new)
        # The rank is effectively (prem-1), so the last column is likely near 0 or ill-defined.
        # We'll keep columns [1 : (prem-1)] for the updated basis in R^p:
        B_trim <- Q_temp[, seq_len((prem - 1)), drop = FALSE]
        # 8) Return both "new_vec" and "B_new" in a single matrix:
        #    - col 1 = new_vec
        #    - cols 2..prem = the newly orthonormalized basis
        output <- matrix(NA_real_, p, prem)
        output[, 1] <- new_vec
        output[, stan_range(2, prem)] <- B_trim  # fill columns 2..prem
        return(output)

      z_beta <- rnorm(length(z_beta), 0, 1)
      # half-Cauchy via <lower=0> and Cauchy(0, scale)
      lambda <- abs(rcauchy(length(lambda), 0, 1))
      tau <- abs(0 + hs_tau0 * rt(length(tau), 3))
      # slab: c2 ~ Inv-Gamma(ν/2, ν s^2/2)
      for (g in seq_len(G)) {
        c2[g] <- 1 / rgamma(1, shape = 0.5 * slab_df, rate = 0.5 * slab_df * slab_scale[g]^2)
      }
      a <- rnorm(1, 0, 1)  # y is z-scored; tighter is fine
      sigma <- abs(0 + 2 * rt(1, 3))
      df <- 2 + abs(2 + 5 * rt(1, 3) - 2)

      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      beta <- rep(NA_real_, d)
      lam2 <- lambda^2
      tau2 <- tau^2
      for (j in seq_len(d)) {
        g <- group[j]
        lam_tilde <- sqrt(c2[g] * lam2[j] / (c2[g] + tau2[g] * lam2[j]))
        beta[j] <- z_beta[j] * tau[g] * lam_tilde
      }

      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#

        p_eff <- p_eff + (1 - kappa[j])

      # R translation of a Stan program, generated by Stan2R (prior predictive simulation).
      # Reads data from the list `dat`; every top-level Stan variable is returned in `out`.
      
      # helper functions
      # fill `like` (a vector, or an array of vectors stored one per row) with draws
      rmulti_normal <- function(like, mu, Sigma) {
        R <- chol(Sigma)
        if (is.matrix(like)) {
          z <- matrix(rnorm(length(like)), nrow(like), ncol(like)) %*% R
          if (is.matrix(mu)) z + mu else sweep(z, 2, mu, "+")
        } else {
          as.vector(mu + rnorm(length(like)) %*% R)
        }
      }
      # onion method (Lewandowski, Kurowicka and Joe 2009); returns the lower Cholesky factor
      rlkj_corr_cholesky <- function(like, eta) {
        K <- nrow(like)
        if (K == 1) return(matrix(1, 1, 1))
        alpha <- eta + (K - 2) / 2
        r12 <- 2 * rbeta(1, alpha, alpha) - 1
        R <- matrix(0, K, K)
        R[1, 1] <- 1
        R[1, 2] <- r12
        R[2, 2] <- sqrt(1 - r12^2)
        if (K > 2) {
          for (m in 2:(K - 1)) {
            alpha <- alpha - 0.5
            y <- rbeta(1, m / 2, alpha)
            z <- rnorm(m)
            R[1:m, m + 1] <- sqrt(y) * z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
            R[m + 1, m + 1] <- sqrt(1 - y)
          }
        }
        t(R)
      }
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      N <- dat$N
      D <- dat$D
      y <- dat$y
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      L <- matrix(NA_real_, D, D)
      L <- rlkj_corr_cholesky(L, 1)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      y <- rmulti_normal(y, rep(0, D), tcrossprod(L))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### generated quantities ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      R <- matrix(NA_real_, D, D)
      R <- tcrossprod(L * lower.tri(L, diag = TRUE))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      out <- list(N = N, D = D, y = y, L = L, R = R)

          log_comp_draws__[[k]] <- rnorm(1, mu, sigma[k])

        x <- c(...)
        m <- max(x)
        if (!is.finite(m)) return(m)
        m + log(sum(exp(x - m)))
      }
      softmax <- function(x) {
        e <- exp(x - max(x))
        e / sum(e)
      }
      # draws from a distribution restricted to [lower, upper] by rejection
      rtruncated_reject <- function(n, draw, lower, upper, max_tries = 1e5) {
        out <- draw(n)
        bad <- out < lower | out > upper
        tries <- 0
        while (any(bad)) {
          tries <- tries + 1
          if (tries > max_tries) stop("rtruncated_reject: no draw inside the bounds after ", max_tries, " tries")
          out[bad] <- draw(n)[bad]
          bad <- out < lower | out > upper
        }
        out
      }

      }

      two_normals_draw__ <- function(y, w, m) {

        y <- switch(component__, rnorm(1, -m, 1), rnorm(1, m, 1))

    Output
      # R translation of a Stan program, generated by Stan2R (prior predictive simulation).
      # Reads data from the list `dat`; every top-level Stan variable is returned in `out`.
      
      # helper functions
      # fill `like` (a vector, or an array of vectors stored one per row) with draws
      rmulti_normal <- function(like, mu, Sigma) {
        R <- chol(Sigma)
        if (is.matrix(like)) {
          z <- matrix(rnorm(length(like)), nrow(like), ncol(like)) %*% R
          if (is.matrix(mu)) z + mu else sweep(z, 2, mu, "+")
        } else {
          as.vector(mu + rnorm(length(like)) %*% R)
        }
      }
      # onion method (Lewandowski, Kurowicka and Joe 2009); returns the lower Cholesky factor
      rlkj_corr_cholesky <- function(like, eta) {
        K <- nrow(like)
        if (K == 1) return(matrix(1, 1, 1))
        alpha <- eta + (K - 2) / 2
        r12 <- 2 * rbeta(1, alpha, alpha) - 1
        R <- matrix(0, K, K)
        R[1, 1] <- 1
        R[1, 2] <- r12
        R[2, 2] <- sqrt(1 - r12^2)
        if (K > 2) {
          for (m in 2:(K - 1)) {
            alpha <- alpha - 0.5
            y <- rbeta(1, m / 2, alpha)
            z <- rnorm(m)
            R[1:m, m + 1] <- sqrt(y) * z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
            R[m + 1, m + 1] <- sqrt(1 - y)
          }
        }
        t(R)
      }
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      N <- dat$N
      K <- dat$K
      y <- dat$y
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      mu <- rep(NA_real_, K)
      tau <- rep(NA_real_, K)
      L <- matrix(NA_real_, K, K)
      mu <- rnorm(length(mu), 0, 1)
      tau <- abs(rcauchy(length(tau), 0, 1))
      L <- rlkj_corr_cholesky(L, 2)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### transformed parameters ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      L_Sigma <- tau * L
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      y <- rmulti_normal(y, mu, tcrossprod(L_Sigma))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### generated quantities ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      Omega <- tcrossprod(L * lower.tri(L, diag = TRUE))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      out <- list(N = N, K = K, y = y, mu = mu, tau = tau, L = L, L_Sigma = L_Sigma,
        Omega = Omega)

      # helper functions
      # P(y = k) = inv_logit(eta - c[k - 1]) - inv_logit(eta - c[k]), with c[0] = -Inf, c[K] = Inf
      rordered_logistic <- function(eta, c) {
        vapply(eta, function(e) {
          p <- -diff(c(1, plogis(e - c), 0))
          sample.int(length(p), 1, prob = p)
        }, numeric(1))
      }

      #### data ####

      x <- dat$x

      c <- rep(NA_real_, K - 1)
      beta <- rnorm(1, 0, 1)
      c <- sort(rnorm(length(c), 0, 2))
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      y <- rordered_logistic(x * beta, c)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      out <- list(N = N, K = K, x = x, y = y, beta = beta, c = c)

        e / sum(e)
      }
      # draws restricted to [lower, upper] by inverse-CDF sampling on the log scale, using
      # whichever tail keeps precision; cdf/quantile accept lower.tail and log.p
      rtruncated <- function(n, cdf, quantile, lower, upper) {
        u <- runif(n)
        ll <- cdf(lower, log.p = TRUE)
        lu <- cdf(upper, log.p = TRUE)
        sl <- cdf(lower, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        su <- cdf(upper, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        suppressWarnings({
          from_lower <- quantile(lu + log(exp(ll - lu) - u * expm1(ll - lu)), log.p = TRUE)
          from_upper <- quantile(sl + log1p(u * expm1(su - sl)), lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        })
        out <- ifelse(ll > log(0.5), from_upper, from_lower)
        if (any(!is.finite(out))) stop("rtruncated: the truncation interval has zero probability")
        out
      }
      # log probability of [lower, upper], computed in the more precise tail
      log_truncated_mass <- function(cdf, lower, upper) {
        ll <- cdf(lower, log.p = TRUE)
        lu <- cdf(upper, log.p = TRUE)
        sl <- cdf(lower, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        su <- cdf(upper, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        ifelse(ll > log(0.5), sl + log1p(-exp(su - sl)), lu + log1p(-exp(ll - lu)))
      }

      #### data ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~#

      total <- dat$total
      count <- dat$count
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#

      lambda <- NA_real_
      lambda <- rlnorm(1, 1, 0.3)
      
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      #### model ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      tail_mass <- sum(pexp(1, lambda, log.p = TRUE))
      for (i in seq_len(n)) {
        # likelihood mixture
        lp_count <- rep(NA_real_, 2)
        lp_count_draws__ <- list()
        lp_count[1] <- log(0.4)
        lp_count_draws__[[1]] <- rbinom(1, total[i], 0.5)
        # theta prior: slab around 0.5 or a spike near either end
        lp_theta <- rep(NA_real_, 3)
        lp_theta_draws__ <- list()
        lp_theta[1] <- log(0.5) + log_truncated_mass(function(q, ...) pnorm(q, 0.5, 0.15, ...), 0, 1)
        lp_theta_draws__[[1]] <- rtruncated(1, function(q, ...) pnorm(q, 0.5, 0.15, ...), function(p, ...) qnorm(p, 0.5, 0.15, ...), 0, 1)

        component__ <- sample.int(length(lp_theta), 1, prob = softmax(lp_theta))

      #### output ####
      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#

      # helper functions
      plaplace <- function(q, mu, sigma) ifelse(q < mu, 0.5 * exp((q - mu) / sigma), 1 - 0.5 * exp(-(q - mu) / sigma))
      qlaplace <- function(p, mu, sigma) ifelse(p < 0.5, mu + sigma * log(2 * p), mu - sigma * log(2 - 2 * p))
      # draws restricted to [lower, upper] by inverse-CDF sampling on the log scale, using
      # whichever tail keeps precision; cdf/quantile accept lower.tail and log.p
      rtruncated <- function(n, cdf, quantile, lower, upper) {

        lu <- cdf(upper, log.p = TRUE)
        sl <- cdf(lower, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        su <- cdf(upper, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        suppressWarnings({
          from_lower <- quantile(lu + log(exp(ll - lu) - u * expm1(ll - lu)), log.p = TRUE)
          from_upper <- quantile(sl + log1p(u * expm1(su - sl)), lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        })
        out <- ifelse(ll > log(0.5), from_upper, from_lower)
        if (any(!is.finite(out))) stop("rtruncated: the truncation interval has zero probability")
        out
      }

      N <- dat$N

      U <- dat$U

      n_half <- trunc(N / 2)
      total <- 0

        } else {

        }

      }

      sigma <- NA_real_
      mu <- qlaplace(plaplace(0, 1, 2) + (1 - plaplace(0, 1, 2)) * runif(1), 1, 2)

      #~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
      
      for (n in seq_len(N)) {

      }

      #### output ####
